source.question: Some people favour this policy. To what extent do you agree?
source.candidateScript:
Public transport plays an important role in modern cities. I agree that governments should invest more in buses and railways, while keeping essential roads in good condition.

Buses can carry much people at the same time. This is good for cities because traffic is a very serious thing. A frequent service could encourage commuters to leave their cars at home, but local authorities need to make the journeys reliable.

Public transport can also give residents more independency. Affordable routes connect residential areas with colleges and workplaces. For example, a student who cannot afford a car could reach an evening course by bus and gain skills for a better job. This shows how transport spending can widen access to education.

However, roads remain important in rural areas. Communities with small populations may not support frequent train services, so road maintenance is needed for buses, deliveries and emergency vehicles. Governments should distinguish essential repairs from expensive urban road expansion.

In conclusion, I support giving public transport a larger share of the budget. Reliable services can reduce pressure on city streets and create more opportunities, while basic road maintenance protects communities that depend on it.
